data.narrative:
Fabri is a robotics and manufacturing company at an undisclosed stage, founded by Steven Davis, Thomas Cole, and Pieter Coulier. The valuation analysis draws from a sector universe of nine comparable companies: one public peer (ticker 277810.KQ) and eight private robotics firms including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics.

The peer-median triangulation method proved inapplicable due to insufficient granular comparables. Although ten same-sector peers exist in robotics and manufacturing, filtering by stage, proximity, and valuation tier yielded fewer than three datapoints in any meaningful subset. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material bias and obscure sector-specific dynamics. Consequently, traditional comparable company valuation cannot be reliably executed with the current dataset.

Without sufficient stage-matched or tier-matched peers, this analysis lacks a quantitative anchor. Further valuation work requires either: (1) expanded data collection on the five identified private peers' recent rounds and valuations; (2) decomposition using cost-of-capital or cash-flow methods if internal financials are available; or (3) staged revaluation once Fabri's funding round closes and market comparables clarify. The single public comparable and broad private peer set are noted but cannot substitute for narrowly filtered multiples at this stage.
